thread:
Kai: Quick idea: introduce a 'soft-rescue' policy UX. It's like autofallback but conservative: sample reroutes, escalate only on sustained error windows, and always present an audit trail.

Nina: Love 'soft-rescue'. How do we avoid thrashing? We need hysteresis and a minimum hold time.

Omar: +1. Also add an emergency_suppress flag so SREs can short-circuit all auto-actions during incident mitigation.

Kai: Proto sketch: mode: soft-rescue | hard-reroute; trigger: composite (5xx_rate, latency_p95, quality_drop); hysteresis_ms; min_hold_s; sample_rate. Audit fields: policy_id, trigger_snapshot, decision_hash, operator_override.

Priya: Console: show a compact timeline with decision dots: green (no action), amber (sampled), red (enforced). Clicking a dot shows sampled inputs (hashed) + top 3 signals. Add a "replay trace" button for simulate.

PolicyBot: policy-engine/pr-88 deployed to staging :white_check_mark: https://ci/p/88

Nina: Telemetry tags: rescue.policy_id, rescue.mode, rescue.decision, rescue.hold_until, rescue.estimate_cost_delta. Include policy_version for auditability.

Omar: For storage: sampled inputs stored encrypted with retention policy; store pointer hash in audit line. Must strip any PII before storing.

Kai: Action items: (1) I'll open proto PR with soft-rescue fields + defaults (dry_run true), (2) Priya: mock timeline with dot-states and replay, (3) Nina: draft telemetry schema, (4) Omar: short runbook for emergency_suppress semantics.

Priya: Will do mocks today. Keep dry_run default for 2 weeks to collect stats.

Kai: Thanks
